nodes.title: Merging dbt source yaml files to preserve existing elements, add new tables, columns
nodes.body:
The data transformation tool dbt uses [source.yaml](https://docs.getdbt.com/docs/building-a-dbt-project/using-sources#testing-and-documenting-sources) files to expose, document and test raw data tables. While there is tooling that will generate fresh yaml that includes any schema changes since it last ran, the original file accumulates additional yaml elements that are typically added manually such as `description`, `tests`, etc.

I have been unable to find the right combination of yq parameters to merge the old file (with accumulated nested metdata) and the new file (that has tables and columns that no longer exist). Either the result is the same as the old file, or it is the same as the new file. I have tried various combinations of:

`yq ea 'select(fileIndex == 0) * select(fileIndex == 1)' original.yaml update.yaml` --results == update.yaml
`yq ea 'select(fileIndex == 0) *? select(fileIndex == 1)' update.yaml original.yaml` --results == original.yaml
`yq ea 'select(fileIndex == 0) *n select(fileIndex == 1)' update.yaml original.yaml` --results == update.yaml

For the moment, I am not concerned with changes such as deleted tables or columns (that would be a great bonus), and I'm only concerned with the `tables:` section of this yaml format.

So for example if I have the following where the original has two tables with descriptive metadata, and then I have an update yaml file that has a new table `customers_orders` and there's also a new column added to `orders` called `creation_timestamp`.

Appreciate any help!

**_original.yaml_**
```
version: 2

sources:
  - name: jaffle_shop
    description: This is a replica of the Postgres database used by our app
    tables:
      - name: customers
        description: One record per customer.
        columns:
          - name: id
            description: Primary key of the customers table
            tests:
              - unique
              - not_null
          - name: email_address
            description: customer email address.
      - name: orders
        description: One record per order. Includes cancelled and deleted orders.
        columns:
          - name: id
            description: Primary key of the orders table
            tests:
              - unique
              - not_null
          - name: status
            description: Note that the status can change over time
```

**_update.yaml_**
```
version: 2

sources:
  - name: jaffle_shop
    description: This is a replica of the Postgres database used by our app
    tables:
      - name: customers
        columns:
          - name: id
          - name: email_address
      - name: customers_orders
        columns:
          - name: customer_id
          - name: order_id
      - name: orders
        columns:
          - name: id
          - name: status
          - name: creation_timestamp
```

**_merged.yaml_**
```
version: 2

sources:
  - name: jaffle_shop
    description: This is a replica of the Postgres database used by our app
    tables:
      - name: customers
        description: One record per customer.
        columns:
          - name: id
            description: Primary key of the customers table
            tests:
              - unique
              - not_null
          - name: email_address
            description: customer email address.
      - name: customers_orders
        columns:
          - name: customer_id
          - name: order_id
      - name: orders
        description: One record per order. Includes cancelled and deleted orders.
        columns:
          - name: id
            description: Primary key of the orders table
            tests:
              - unique
              - not_null
          - name: status
            description: Note that the status can change over time
          - name: creation_timestamp
```
